question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person or entity that is unable to pay debts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Insolvent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "insolvent" is a person or entity that is unable to pay their debts (i.e., whose liabilities exceed assets and who cannot meet financial obligations). (दिवालिया)

◦ Example: After heavy losses, the company was declared insolvent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Busted" (informal — broken / caught) is not a formal one-word substitute for this meaning.

• Option 2 "Insurgent" means a rebel who rises against authority.

• Option 4 "Recluse" means a person who lives alone and avoids society.

NOTE

• Related legal terms: bankrupt (declared insolvent by a court), solvent (able to pay debts — the antonym), liquidation (winding up an insolvent company). India's Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) was enacted in 2016.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

The meteorological department predicted heavy rain over the coming days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Light.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heavy" (of rain) means falling in large amounts; intense. Its antonym is "light", meaning gentle and small in amount. (भारी का विलोम — हल्का)

◦ Example: The heavy rain of yesterday gave way to a light drizzle today.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Drizzly" describes fine, light rain but is not the direct antonym of "heavy".

• Option 3 "Plentiful" (in large quantity) is closer to a synonym.

• Option 4 "Rare" (uncommon) refers to frequency, not intensity.

NOTE

• Collocations with "heavy": heavy rain, heavy traffic, heavy meal, heavy loss. Antonym pairs: heavy ↔ light, dense ↔ sparse.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

Only the beautiful painting is to be displayed in the exhibition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the most beautiful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Selecting a single item out of many for display implies the highest degree, so the superlative "the most beautiful" is required. (सर्वोत्तम — अतिशयोकर्ष)

◦ Correct: Only the most beautiful painting is to be displayed in the exhibition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more beautiful" (comparative) needs "than" and is used to compare only two things.

• Option 3 "the much beautiful" is grammatically wrong — "much" is not used with countable adjectives this way.

• Option 4 "beautiful" (positive degree) does not convey that one painting is picked as the best.

NOTE

• Degrees of "beautiful": beautiful – more beautiful (than) – the most beautiful. Long adjectives take "more/most", not "-er/-est".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

We / enjoyed lunch / he gave / us.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. enjoyed lunch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "lunch" here is specified by the relative clause "(that) he gave us", so it needs the definite article "the". The segment should read "enjoyed the lunch". (निश्चित उपपद 'the' आवश्यक)

◦ Correct: We enjoyed the lunch (that) he gave us.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "We", "he gave" and "us" are all correct.

• The relative pronoun "that/which" is optional here (a contact clause), but the article "the" is compulsory because the lunch is a particular one.

NOTE

• Use "the" before a noun that is made specific/definite by a following clause or phrase: "the book I bought", "the man who called".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He couldn't attend the meeting _________ he was sick.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. because.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Because" introduces the reason/cause. His sickness is the reason he could not attend, so "because" fits. (क्योंकि — कारण)

◦ Correct: He couldn't attend the meeting because he was sick.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "so" shows a result, not a cause, and would need re-ordering.

• Option 3 "although" shows contrast/concession (opposite idea), which does not fit.

• Option 4 "but" is a coordinating conjunction of contrast and cannot join a reason clause here.

NOTE

• Conjunctions of reason: because, since, as, for. Conjunctions of contrast: although, though, even though, but, yet.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Please bring two bananas and the piece of cake from the market.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. and the piece of cake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Piece of cake" is being mentioned for the first time and is non-specific, so it needs the indefinite article "a", not "the". It should be "a piece of cake". (अनिश्चित उपपद 'a' चाहिए)

◦ Correct: Please bring two bananas and a piece of cake from the market.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Please bring", "two bananas" and "from the market" are all correct.

• "the market" is fine because it refers to a particular, known market.

NOTE

• Use "a/an" for a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time or that is one of many; use "the" for something specific/already known.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Despite their differences, the counties found common ground and buried the hatchet.
option_4: To seek revenge in the future
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To settle a dispute peacefully.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to make peace; to end a quarrel and become friendly again, i.e., to settle a dispute peacefully. (सुलह कर लेना / झगड़ा समाप्त करना)

◦ Example: The two brothers finally decided to bury the hatchet and work together.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (continue conflict, disagree publicly, seek revenge) are all opposite to the idiom's meaning of reconciliation.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from a Native American custom of literally burying weapons (a hatchet/axe) to mark the end of hostilities. Similar idioms: "make peace", "call a truce", "mend fences".

question: Identify the sentence with the adverbial error.
option_1: She ran the marathon fast incredibly.
option_2: She ran the marathon incredibly fast.
option_3: She ran incredibly the marathon fast.
option_4: She ran the incredibly marathon fast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. She ran the marathon incredibly fast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Option 2 shows the correct placement of adverbs. The intensifying adverb "incredibly" modifies the adverb of manner "fast", so the natural order is "incredibly fast", placed after the object "the marathon". (क्रियाविशेषण का सही क्रम)

◦ Correct: She ran the marathon incredibly fast.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fast incredibly" wrongly reverses the two adverbs.

• Option 3 "ran incredibly the marathon fast" wrongly splits the verb from its object.

• Option 4 "the incredibly marathon" wrongly puts the adverb before a noun (marathon).

NOTE

• Order rule: an adverb of degree (incredibly, very, extremely) comes before the word it intensifies (incredibly fast, very quickly). Adverbs of manner usually follow the verb + object.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The impacts of climate change on different sectors of society are interelated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. interrelated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "interrelated", meaning connected or related to one another. The prefix "inter-" (between/among) is followed by "related" — giving a double 'r': INTER + RELATED. (परस्पर संबंधित)

◦ Correct: The impacts of climate change on different sectors of society are interrelated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "interreleted", "enterrelated" (wrong "enter") and "interrilated" all have wrong vowels/letters.

NOTE

• Words with the prefix "inter-" (between): international, interact, intervene, interconnect. Note the double 'r' in interrelated and interregnum.

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: This is a very difficult task to accomplish.
option_2: A young boy offered her his seat.
option_3: I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.
option_4: I have a lot of work to complete.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eraser" is a singular countable noun used for the first time, so it needs the indefinite article "an" (before the vowel sound). It should be "I wish I had an eraser". (अनिश्चित उपपद 'an' छूट गया)

◦ Correct: I wish I had an eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are grammatically correct.

• "an" is used (not "a") because "eraser" begins with a vowel sound.

NOTE

• Countable singular nouns must take a determiner (a/an/the/my/this...). Use "an" before words starting with a vowel sound: an eraser, an hour, an umbrella.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Rahul speaks fluently English / although he makes / quite a lot of mistakes / while writing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rahul speaks fluently English.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb of manner "fluently" is wrongly placed between the verb and its object. It should come after the object: "speaks English fluently". (क्रिया + कर्म के बाद क्रियाविशेषण)

◦ Correct: Rahul speaks English fluently although he makes quite a lot of mistakes while writing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "although he makes", "quite a lot of mistakes" and "while writing" are all correct.

NOTE

• Word order rule: a verb should not be separated from its direct object by an adverb. Say "speaks English fluently", "plays the guitar beautifully" — object first, then the adverb of manner.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Proficient
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Accomplished.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Proficient" means highly skilled; expert at doing something. Its closest synonym is "accomplished" (highly skilled/talented). (निपुण / कुशल)

◦ Example: She is a proficient/accomplished pianist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Glamorous" (attractive/charming) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Callous" (unfeeling/insensitive) is unrelated.

• Option 4 "Recalcitrant" (stubbornly disobedient) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of proficient: skilled, expert, adept, competent, accomplished. Antonyms: incompetent, unskilled, inept.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fatigued
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tired.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fatigued" means extremely tired; exhausted; weary. Its closest synonym is "tired". (थका हुआ)

◦ Example: After the long march, the soldiers were completely fatigued/tired.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Furious" (very angry), Option 3 "Tricky" (difficult/deceptive) and Option 4 "Famous" (well known) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fatigued: tired, exhausted, weary, worn out, drained. Antonyms: energetic, fresh, refreshed, invigorated.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

As the orchestra played, the audience was mesmerised by the beautiful melodies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. abstracted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mesmerised" means spellbound; completely holding one's attention; fascinated. Its antonym is "abstracted", meaning inattentive, absent-minded, lost in thought (i.e., NOT paying attention). (मंत्रमुग्ध का विलोम — अन्यमनस्क / ध्यान न देने वाला)

◦ Example: While the others were mesmerised by the music, he sat abstracted, gazing out of the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "alienated" (estranged/isolated), Option 2 "dirty" and Option 3 "turbid" (cloudy/muddy) do not express the opposite of "fascinated/attentive".

NOTE

• Synonyms of mesmerised: fascinated, spellbound, captivated, enthralled. Antonym "abstracted" = distracted, inattentive, preoccupied.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

His dog did not _________ when thieves were slashing the _________ of his precious tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bark.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A dog "barks" — the correct verb for the sound a dog makes. The sentence needs a word for what the dog failed to do when thieves came, i.e., "did not bark". (भौंकना)

◦ Correct: His dog did not bark when thieves were slashing the stem/bark of his precious tree.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "shout" is used for humans, not the sound a dog makes.

• Option 3 "stem" and Option 4 "claw" are nouns and do not fit as the verb the dog performs.

NOTE

• Note the pun: "bark" is both the sound a dog makes and the outer covering of a tree. Animal sounds: dogs bark, cats mew, cows moo, lions roar, horses neigh.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

If you don't have a lump sum to ______ in a fixed deposit, you can surely opt for a long-term recurring deposit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. invest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Invest" means to put money into a scheme/asset to earn a return. One "invests" a lump sum in a fixed deposit. (निवेश करना)

◦ Correct: If you don't have a lump sum to invest in a fixed deposit, you can surely opt for a long-term recurring deposit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gather" (to collect), Option 3 "publish" (to print/issue) and Option 4 "draw" (to pull/withdraw) do not collocate with "in a fixed deposit".

NOTE

• Finance vocabulary: fixed deposit (FD) — a lump sum kept for a fixed term at a fixed interest; recurring deposit (RD) — a fixed amount deposited every month. Collocation: "invest in" something.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Green thumb
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Being good at growing plants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "green thumb" (British: "green fingers") means a natural talent or skill for gardening and growing plants. (बागवानी में निपुण होना)

◦ Example: My grandmother has a real green thumb — her garden is always in full bloom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (corruption, visiting a market, preparing for war) have no connection with the idiom.

NOTE

• "Green thumb" (American English) = "green fingers" (British English). Related colour idioms: "red tape" (bureaucracy), "blue blood" (aristocracy), "caught red-handed".

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful.

Sheetal has been studying engineering for five years, ____________________ countless hours to her coursework.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. dedicating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "dedicating", from "dedicate" — to devote (time/effort) wholly to a purpose. Spelling key: DE + DI + CA + TING. (समर्पित करना)

◦ Correct: Sheetal has been studying engineering for five years, dedicating countless hours to her coursework.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "dedecating", "deddicating" (double 'd') and "daidicating" all use wrong vowels/letters.

NOTE

• Related words: dedicate (verb), dedicated (adjective — devoted), dedication (noun). "Dedicate to" a cause/purpose.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.

His performace in the play was outstanding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. performace.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Performace" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "performance" (with an 'n' before the 'c'): PER + FORM + ANCE. (प्रदर्शन — सही वर्तनी performance)

◦ Correct: His performance in the play was outstanding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "play", "outstanding" and "His" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Root "perform" + suffix "-ance" = performance. Similar "-ance" nouns: importance, appearance, maintenance, attendance.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Exactly the same words as were used originally.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Verbatim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Verbatim" means in exactly the same words as were used originally; word for word. (शब्दशः / अक्षरशः)

◦ Example: The reporter quoted the minister's speech verbatim.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Factual" (based on facts), Option 2 "Ornate" (highly decorated) and Option 3 "Precise" (exact/accurate) do not carry the specific meaning of "word for word".

NOTE

• "Verbatim" works as both an adverb and an adjective. Related: literal (word for word / exact), paraphrase (restate in different words — the opposite idea).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation's dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. his.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sniffer dog Tucker is referred to throughout the passage with the masculine pronoun "He" ("He searches for whale faeces..."). So the possessive adjective for his nose must be "his". (उसका — नर के लिए)

◦ Correct: Sniffer dog Tucker uses his nose to help researchers ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "its" would be used only if the dog were treated as a genderless animal, but the passage uses "He/his".

• Options 3 "him" (object pronoun) and 4 "her" (feminine) do not agree with "He".

NOTE

• Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. They come before a noun (his nose) and must agree with the person/thing they refer to.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation's dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed phrase "on the decline" means decreasing / becoming smaller in number or size. The killer whale population is "on the decline". (गिरावट पर / घट रहा)

◦ Correct: ... a killer whale population ... is on the decline.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "at", 2 "after" and 3 "off" do not form the standard collocation with "the decline".

NOTE

• Useful prepositional phrases: "on the rise" (increasing), "on the decline / on the wane" (decreasing), "on the mend" (recovering).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation's dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A number of species" means several/various species. The dogs are used by scientists studying "a number of species" including right whales and killer whales. (एक संख्या / कई)

◦ Correct: ... scientists studying a number of species including right whales and killer whales.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cacophony" (harsh mixture of sounds) does not fit "species".

• Option 2 "cadre" (a core group of trained people) is used for people, not species.

• Option 4 "division" would need "into" and changes the meaning.

NOTE

• "A number of + plural noun" = several/many (takes a plural verb). Compare with "the number of" (which takes a singular verb).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation's dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. based.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An organisation that has its main location in a place is said to be "based" there. Working Dogs for Conservation is "based in Three Forks, Montana". (स्थित / मुख्यालय वाला)

◦ Correct: ... Working Dogs for Conservation, based in Three Forks, Montana.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "surviving" and Option 3 "living" are used for living beings, not the location of an organisation.

• Option 4 "rested" does not fit the sense of location.

NOTE

• Collocation: an organisation/company is "based in" a city/country (headquartered there). Example: "a firm based in Mumbai".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation's dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. longer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "no longer" means not any more. So many new projects have sprung up that Hurt can "no longer keep track of them all" — she cannot do so any more. (अब और नहीं)

◦ Correct: ... Hurt can no longer keep track of them all.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "lesser", Option 3 "moreover" and Option 4 "shorter" do not combine with "no" to give the meaning "not any more".

NOTE

• "No longer" = not any more (of time): "He no longer works here." Compare "no more" (quantity). Both express that something has stopped.

question: Who is the author of 'Temple Tales: Secrets & Stories of India's Sacred Places'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sudha G Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Temple Tales: Secrets & Stories of India's Sacred Places" was written by the journalist and author Sudha G Tilak. The book explores the legends, myths and histories behind famous Indian temples. (सुधा जी तिलक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shashi Tharoor is a well-known politician-author (An Era of Darkness, The Great Indian Novel).

• Mulk Raj Anand was a pioneer of Indian English fiction (Untouchable, Coolie).

NOTE

• Books on Indian temples and culture are a recurring theme in SSC static/current-affairs GK; note authors along with their major works.

question: Who among the following is the author of the book named 'Streepurushtulna'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tarabai Shinde.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stri Purush Tulana (Streepurushtulna)" — a comparison of men and women — was written by Tarabai Shinde in 1882. It is regarded as the first modern Indian feminist text, criticising patriarchy and caste. (ताराबाई शिंदे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tarabai Shinde was a social reformer associated with the Satyashodhak Samaj of Jyotirao Phule.

• Pandit Ramabai wrote "The High-Caste Hindu Woman"; Rassundari Devi wrote "Amar Jiban", the first full-length autobiography in Bengali.

NOTE

• Sarojini Naidu, the "Nightingale of India", was a poet (The Golden Threshold) and the first Indian woman President of the INC and first woman Governor (UP).

question: Squash player Anahat Singh belongs to which city in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The young Indian squash prodigy Anahat Singh belongs to Delhi. She has become one of India's most promising squash players, winning several junior international titles. (अनाहत सिंह — दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anahat Singh was part of India's squash contingent at the Asian Games and Commonwealth Games, and won a gold medal in the mixed doubles at the 2022 Commonwealth Games junior/senior events era of Indian squash.

• Squash is played in a four-walled court with a small rubber ball and rackets.

NOTE

• India's leading squash players include Saurav Ghosal, Dipika Pallikal, Joshna Chinappa and the rising star Anahat Singh.

question: In September 2023, at the BRICS Innovation Forum in Moscow, who among the following, who is a Chief Innovation Officer from Telangana, received the World Innovation Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanta Thoutam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shanta Thoutam, the Chief Innovation Officer of Telangana, received the World Innovation Award at the BRICS Innovation Forum held in Moscow in September 2023. (शांता थौताम — तेलंगाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The award recognised Telangana's innovation ecosystem and initiatives such as T-Hub, WE-Hub and T-Works.

• BRICS is a grouping of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (later expanded to include more members).

NOTE

• KT Rama Rao (KTR) and K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) are prominent Telangana political leaders (BRS party); do not confuse them with the innovation officer.

question: Which of the following is considered unicellular green algae?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlamydomonas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chlamydomonas" is a unicellular (single-celled) green alga. It is a common example of a motile, flagellated green alga used widely in biology to study photosynthesis and genetics. (क्लैमाइडोमोनस — एककोशिकीय हरित शैवाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Oedogonium and Cladophora are filamentous (multicellular) green algae.

• Chlorophyta is the entire division (phylum) of green algae, not a single organism.

NOTE

• Green algae belong to the division Chlorophyta and contain chlorophyll a and b. Other examples: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Volvox, Chlorella.

question: Which of the following temples is NOT an example of Nagara style of architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kailasha temple, Kanchipuram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram (Tamil Nadu) is built in the Dravida (South Indian) style, NOT the Nagara style. It was built by the Pallava rulers. (कैलासनाथ मंदिर, कांचीपुरम — द्रविड़ शैली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lingaraja temple (Bhubaneswar), Kandariya Mahadeva temple (Khajuraho, MP) and the Sun Temple (Konark, Odisha) are all classic examples of Nagara (North Indian) architecture with a curvilinear shikhara.

NOTE

• Indian temple styles: Nagara (North India — curved shikhara), Dravida (South India — pyramidal vimana with gopurams), and Vesara (a mix of both, found in the Deccan).

question: Which of the following Union Territories has the lowest population as per the Census of India 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshdweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Lakshadweep had the lowest population among all States and Union Territories, with only about 64,473 people. (लक्षद्वीप — सबसे कम जनसंख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lakshadweep is also the smallest Union Territory by area.

• Sikkim has the lowest population among the states.

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state; among UTs, Delhi was the most populous in 2011.

NOTE

• 2011 Census facts: most populous state UP, least populous state Sikkim; largest state by area Rajasthan; UT with lowest population Lakshadweep.

question: Which of the following pollutants is responsible for the acidification of ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide (CO2).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ocean acidification is caused mainly by carbon dioxide (CO₂). When excess CO₂ from the atmosphere dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), lowering the pH of the ocean. (महासागरीय अम्लीकरण — CO₂)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The reaction: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid) → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻, increasing acidity.

• Ocean acidification harms coral reefs and shell-forming organisms by dissolving calcium carbonate.

NOTE

• CO₂ is also the chief greenhouse gas causing global warming. Note: SO₂ and NOₓ cause acid rain, while CO₂ causes ocean acidification.

question: Which of the following is NOT a religious festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi Jayanti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gandhi Jayanti" is NOT a religious festival — it is a national event observed on 2nd October to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. (गांधी जयंती — राष्ट्रीय दिवस, धार्मिक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Guru Purab (Sikh — birth anniversary of the Gurus, esp. Guru Nanak), Good Friday (Christian — commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus) and Muharram (Islamic) are all religious festivals.

NOTE

• Gandhi Jayanti (2 October) is one of India's three national holidays, along with Republic Day (26 January) and Independence Day (15 August). The UN also observes it as the International Day of Non-Violence.

question: Dhamma is the __________ word for the Sanskrit word 'Dharma'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prakrit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dhamma" is the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit word "Dharma". Emperor Ashoka used the term "Dhamma" (a moral code of conduct) in his edicts, which were largely written in Prakrit. (धम्म — प्राकृत शब्द)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ashoka's edicts were mostly written in Prakrit language using the Brahmi script.

• Ashoka's Dhamma promoted non-violence, tolerance, respect for elders and moral living, after the Kalinga War (261 BCE).

NOTE

• Prakrit was the common spoken language of ancient India, while Sanskrit was the classical, scholarly language. Pali (a form of Prakrit) is the language of Buddhist Tripitaka texts.

question: Which of the following is the headquarter of East Central Railway?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hajipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The headquarters of the East Central Railway (ECR) zone is at Hajipur (Bihar). (पूर्व मध्य रेलवे — हाजीपुर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The East Central Railway was formed in 2002 and covers parts of Bihar and Jharkhand.

• Indian Railways is divided into zones, each headed by a General Manager.

NOTE

• Some zonal HQs: Northern Railway – New Delhi; Eastern – Kolkata; Western – Mumbai; Southern – Chennai; North Eastern Frontier – Guwahati; East Central – Hajipur.

question: According to Koeppen's Scheme of climatic regions of India, in which of the following states is the 'BWhw' and 'BShw' type climate found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Koeppen's classification, the "BWhw" (hot desert) and "BShw" (hot semi-arid/steppe) climates are found in Rajasthan (the Thar Desert region and its surroundings). (राजस्थान — मरुस्थलीय जलवायु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In Koeppen's scheme, "B" stands for dry climates; "W" = desert, "S" = steppe; "h" = hot; "w" = dry winter.

• BWhw = hot desert (western Rajasthan); BShw = hot semi-arid (eastern Rajasthan, Punjab, parts of Gujarat/Haryana).

NOTE

• Wladimir Koeppen classified climates using temperature and precipitation. Main groups: A (tropical), B (dry), C (warm temperate), D (cold), E (ice/polar).

question: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 11 August 2023, which amends the ________________________.
option_1: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017
option_2: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2016
option_3: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2014
option_4: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2015
solution_text:
The correct answer is Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 amends the IGST Act, 2017. It was introduced to bring the taxation of online money gaming, casinos and horse racing under the GST framework. (आईजीएसटी अधिनियम, 2017)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• GST was rolled out in India on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.

• GST has components: CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST — IGST applies to inter-state supplies and imports.

NOTE

• The GST Council (headed by the Union Finance Minister) is the apex body for GST decisions in India. GST is a destination-based, multi-stage indirect tax.

question: According to the Census of India 2001, how much percentage of the immigrant population was from Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.9%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2001, about 2.9% of the immigrant population in India was from Sri Lanka. (श्रीलंका से — 2.9%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The largest share of immigrants to India has traditionally come from neighbouring countries such as Bangladesh, Pakistan and Nepal.

• Migration in census data is studied by place of birth and place of last residence.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years (decennial). The first synchronous census was in 1881; census work is under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

question: VP Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan were honoured with Rukminidevi Memorial Award in 2009 for which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The celebrated dancer couple V. P. Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan ("The Dhananjayans") are exponents of Bharatanatyam and were honoured with the Rukmini Devi Memorial Award in 2009. (भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The award is named after Rukmini Devi Arundale, who revived and popularised Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra in Chennai.

• The Dhananjayans have also received the Padma Bhushan.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra. The eight classical dance forms are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: The Shuddhi Movement to reconvert to the Hindu fold the converts to other religions, was started by which of the following organisations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Shuddhi Movement" — aimed at reconverting to Hinduism those who had converted to other religions — was started by the Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati. (आर्य समाज — शुद्धि आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 at Bombay by Swami Dayananda Saraswati, who gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas".

• It opposed idol worship, caste rigidity and untouchability, and promoted widow remarriage and women's education.

NOTE

• Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1828); Satyashodhak Samaj by Jyotirao Phule (1873); Dharma Sabha by Radhakanta Deb (1830), an orthodox body opposing reforms.

question: To which state does Indian shooter Abhinav Bindra belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ace Indian shooter Abhinav Bindra was born in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. He won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the 10 m Air Rifle event at the Beijing Olympics 2008. (अभिनव बिंद्रा — उत्तराखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Abhinav Bindra has been honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Padma Bhushan and Arjuna Award.

• His autobiography is titled "A Shot at History".

NOTE

• India's individual Olympic gold medallists: Abhinav Bindra (Shooting, 2008) and Neeraj Chopra (Javelin, Tokyo 2020).

question: Which of the following was NOT found in the Harappan excavation sites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public hospital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Public hospital" was NOT found in the excavations of the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilization. Its cities show houses, public buildings and baths but no evidence of hospitals. (सार्वजनिक अस्पताल नहीं मिला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Harappan sites revealed well-planned dwelling houses, the Great Bath (public bath) at Mohenjo-daro, granaries, and public buildings.

• The civilization is famous for its grid-pattern town planning, drainage system and standardised burnt bricks.

NOTE

• Major Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal (dockyard), Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi. The civilization flourished around 2500 BCE along the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra rivers.

question:
Which of the following are the major objectives of governments engaged in the budgetary process in India?
a. Stabilising the level of aggregate demand in the economy
b. Redistributing incomes of people as per constitutional principles
c. Floating schemes to appeal to citizens in a democratic way on a regular basis
d. Allocating funds to various economic activities
option_2: All a, b, c and d
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only a and b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the given options, the major objectives selected are (a) stabilising the level of aggregate demand in the economy and (b) redistributing incomes of people as per constitutional principles. (केवल a और b)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three broad functions of a government budget are: the allocation function, the redistribution function and the stabilisation function.

• Stabilisation aims to control inflation/deflation and maintain full employment; redistribution reduces income inequality through taxes and subsidies.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement". It has two parts — the Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget.

question: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the procedure of making amendments in the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Constitution borrowed the procedure for amendment of the Constitution and the election of members of the Rajya Sabha from the Constitution of South Africa. (संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया — दक्षिण अफ्रीका से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amendment of the Constitution is dealt with under Article 368.

• From Australia: Concurrent List, freedom of trade, joint sitting of Parliament.

• From Ireland: Directive Principles, nomination of Rajya Sabha members, method of Presidential election.

NOTE

• Other borrowings: USA – Fundamental Rights, judicial review; UK – parliamentary system, rule of law; Canada – federation with a strong Centre; USSR – Fundamental Duties, Five-Year Plans.

question: The structure of methanol is CH3OH. This kind of representation is known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is condensed structural formula.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Writing methanol as "CH₃OH" is a "condensed structural formula" — the atoms are shown grouped together without drawing all the individual bonds, to save space. (संघनित संरचना सूत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Complete (expanded) structural formula shows all atoms and all bonds separately.

• Bond-line (skeletal) formula represents carbon chains as zig-zag lines with carbons at the vertices.

• Wedge-and-dash representation shows the 3-D orientation of bonds.

NOTE

• Methanol (CH₃OH) is the simplest alcohol; it is toxic and used as a solvent and fuel. Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is the alcohol present in alcoholic drinks.

question: Lachhu Maharaj has been associated with which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lachhu Maharaj was a renowned exponent and choreographer of the Kathak classical dance form, belonging to the famous Lucknow gharana. (लच्छू महाराज — कथक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak has three main gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Other Kathak legends include Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj and Sitara Devi.

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India, marked by fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and storytelling. The word "Kathak" comes from "katha" (story).

question: Which raga was composed by music emperor Mian Tansen to bring rain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Megh Malhar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The raga "Megh Malhar" is traditionally believed to have been sung by Mian Tansen to bring rain. It is a monsoon raga associated with clouds and rainfall. (मेघ मल्हार — वर्षा के लिए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tansen was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar.

• Another legend holds that Tansen sang Raga Deepak which produced fire/heat.

NOTE

• Ragas in Indian classical music are associated with particular times/seasons and moods: Malhar (monsoon/rain), Bhairav (morning), Deepak (fire), Bahar (spring).

question: Muscle cells and muscle fibres are developed from embryonic precursor cells known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is myoblasts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Muscle cells and muscle fibres develop from embryonic precursor cells called "myoblasts". Myoblasts fuse together during development to form multinucleated muscle fibres. (मायोब्लास्ट — पेशी की पूर्ववर्ती कोशिकाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A "myocyte" is a mature muscle cell.

• A "myofibril" is a thread-like contractile unit inside a muscle fibre.

• "Myonuclei" are the nuclei present within muscle fibres.

NOTE

• There are three types of muscle: skeletal (striated, voluntary), smooth (unstriated, involuntary) and cardiac (heart) muscle. The contractile proteins in muscle are actin and myosin.

question: The Constitution of India has borrowed many provisions from different countries as well as from the Government of India Act of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1935.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution of India borrowed a large number of provisions from the Government of India Act, 1935, including the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, public service commissions and emergency provisions. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for an All-India Federation and provincial autonomy, and introduced bicameralism in some provinces.

• Nearly 250 articles of the Indian Constitution are said to be based on this Act.

NOTE

• Other landmark Acts: Regulating Act 1773, Government of India Act 1858, Indian Councils Acts, Morley-Minto (1909), Montagu-Chelmsford / GOI Act 1919, and GOI Act 1935.
